exclusion_quote: Dissertation at Uppsala University to be publicly examined in Polhemsalen, Ångström-laboratoriet, Thursday, September 23, 2004 at 10:15 for the Degree of Doctor of Philosophy.
exclusion_location: main, PDF p. 2 (abstract page following the title page)

I1.quote: The isotherms were measured at three temperatures (77, 195 and 300 K) in a UHV compatible Sievert's apparatus.

I2.quote: The hydrogen uptake of two nanostructured carbon based materials denoted Multi-Walled Nano-Barrels (MWNB) and Amorphous Nanoporous Carbon (ANPC) was explored.

I3.quote: The maximum hydrogen uptake at 77 K and hydrogen pressure of 10 MPa was determined to be 4.2 and 6.2 wt.% for ANPC and MWNB, respectively.

I4.quote: The resulting materials exhibited a high porosity and large specific surface area (1000 m2 ·g for ANPC and 600 m2 ·g for MWNB)

I5.quote: The dissociative and non-dissociative hydrogen uptake in carbon nanostructures and metallic films were investigated by measurements and analysis of solubility isotherms.

notes: The document is a PhD thesis: Uppsala 'Comprehensive Summaries of Uppsala Dissertations' no. 1005 (summary only; the six papers are not reprinted in the file). It is excluded as not_primary by document type. I1 to I5 are each met on the thesis text itself: the H2 uptake values for the carbon samples (ANPC, MWNB) are the author's own volumetric (Sieverts) measurements summarised from Paper I (J. Alloy Comp. 330-332, 670 (2002)); the surface areas carry a '1000 m2·g' unit typo for m2/g; the BET-N2 method is named in Section 3.3.1 (main, p. 35, PDF p. 43). Section 3.3.1 lists measurement temperatures 298, 152 and 77 K while Section 4.1 lists 77, 195 and 300 K (internal inconsistency). duplicate_data was not coded: the thesis says it is based on published papers but does not state that every uptake value was published before, and not_primary precedes it in the code order.
